Meeting Title: API latency incident review
Meeting Date: 2026-10-23

Mei Tan: Mei Tan: Let's anchor the discussion on scope and expected outcome. What has actually changed since the last check-in?
Andre Lewis: Andre Lewis: The current picture is the service recovered after connection-pool limits were reduced. We have the incident window lasted 27 minutes and affected roughly 8 percent of requests, and the signal I am watching is p95 latency peaked at 4.8 seconds while the worker queue was saturated.
Sofia Martinez: Sofia Martinez: My concern is the same queue pressure could recur during the next scheduled import. If the operations team needs to approve the alert threshold, what do we tell the people relying on this work?
Caleb Turner: Caleb Turner: We can add queue-depth alerts and cap concurrent imports before increasing pool size. We should keep whether a second worker pool is needed for long-running imports visible until that check is complete.
Mei Tan: Mei Tan: For the record, treat queue saturation as the primary contributing factor and track the database limit as a contributing condition. Andre Lewis will add a queue-depth alert and run a controlled load test before the next high-volume import window; whether a second worker pool is needed for long-running imports remains unresolved.
